{{Short description|Quantum information quantity}}
{{Orphan|date=July 2026}}

'''Reflected entropy''' is a quantity in [[quantum information]] theory that measures [[correlation]]s in a bipartite [[Quantum mechanics|quantum-mechanical]] system described by a [[Mixed state (physics)|mixed state]]. It is defined by constructing a canonical [[Purification of quantum state|purification]] of the [[density matrix]] in an enlarged [[Hilbert space]] and computing the [[Entropy of entanglement|entanglement entropy]] between the two subsystems in this purified state. Reflected entropy provides a way to characterize both classical and quantum correlations and is closely related to other information-theoretic quantities such as [[Mutual information]].

In the context of the holographic [[AdS/CFT correspondence]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maldacena |first=Juan |date=1998 |title=The large $N$ limit of superconformal field theories and supergravity |url=https://link.intlpress.com/JDetail/1805563384005337090 |journal=Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=231–252 |doi=10.4310/ATMP.1998.v2.n2.a1 |bibcode=1998AdTMP...2..231M }}</ref> reflected entropy for a pair of spatial regions in a [[conformal field theory]] (CFT) is conjectured to be related to a geometric quantity in the dual [[Anti-de Sitter space|anti-de Sitter]] (AdS) spacetime. Specifically, it has been proposed that the reflected entropy is proportional to the area of a minimal surface associated with the two regions in the bulk spacetime, extending the ideas of the [[Ryu–Takayanagi conjecture|Ryu-Takayanagi formula]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ryu |first1=Shinsei |last2=Takayanagi |first2=Tadashi |date=2006-05-09 |title=Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from the anti–de Sitter Space/Conformal Field Theory Correspondence |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.181602 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=96 |issue=18 |article-number=181602 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.181602 |pmid=16712357 |arxiv=hep-th/0603001 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..96r1602R |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> to mixed states. This relation, sometimes referred to as the [[Dutta-Faulkner formula]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Dutta |first1=Souvik |last2=Faulkner |first2=Thomas |date=2021-03-18 |title=A canonical purification for the entanglement wedge cross-section |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP03(2021)178 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2021 |issue=3 |pages=178 |doi=10.1007/JHEP03(2021)178 |bibcode=2021JHEP...03..178D |issn=1029-8479|arxiv=1905.00577 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hayden |first1=Patrick |last2=Parrikar |first2=Onkar |last3=Sorce |first3=Jonathan |date=2021-10-06 |title=The Markov gap for geometric reflected entropy |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP10(2021)047 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2021 |issue=10 |pages=47 |doi=10.1007/JHEP10(2021)047 |arxiv=2107.00009 |bibcode=2021JHEP...10..047H |issn=1029-8479}}</ref> provides a connection between quantum information measures in the CFT and geometric structures in the dual gravitational description.

== Conjecture ==
Consider a bipartite system consisting of two disjoint boundary regions <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> in a CFT. In the holographic setting, the union <math>A\cup B</math> is associated with an entanglement wedge<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Headrick |first1=Matthew |last2=Hubeny |first2=Veronika E. |last3=Lawrence |first3=Albion |last4=Rangamani |first4=Mukund |date=2014-12-29 |title=Causality & holographic entanglement entropy |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/JHEP12(2014)162 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2014 |issue=12 |pages=162 |doi=10.1007/JHEP12(2014)162 |arxiv=1408.6300 |bibcode=2014JHEP...12..162H |issn=1029-8479}}</ref> in the dual spacetime. Within this region <math>\mathcal{W}_{A\cup B}</math>, the entanglement wedge cross-section <math>E_\mathcal{W}</math> is defined as the minimal-area [[codimension]]-2 surface that splits <math>\mathcal{W}_{A\cup B}</math>. The surface <math>E_\mathcal{W}</math> satisfies several important properties:

# <math>E_\mathcal{W}</math> lies entirely within <math>\mathcal{W}_{A\cup B}</math>
# Its area is non-decreasing under the inclusion of additional boundary regions: <math>E_{\mathcal{W}'} > E_\mathcal{W} \text{ if } \mathcal{W}' \supset \mathcal W</math>
# <math>E_\mathcal{W}</math> reduces to the minimal Ryu–Takayanagi surface for either <math>A</math> or '''<math>B</math>''' when <math>A\cup B</math> is a pure quantum state.

The reflected entropy <math>S_R(A:B)</math> is given by

<math>\frac{1}{2}S_R(A:B) = \frac{\text{Area}(E_\mathcal{W})}{4G_N}</math>,

where <math>G_N </math> is Newton's gravitational constant. The reflected entropy was proposed by Souvik Dutta and Thomas Faulkner in 2019,<ref name=":0" /> and generalizes the Ryu–Takayanagi prescription to mixed states, providing an alternative to the entanglement of purification proposal of [[Tadashi Takayanagi|Takayanagi]] and Umemoto.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Umemoto |first1=Koji |last2=Takayanagi |first2=Tadashi |date=June 2018 |title=Entanglement of purification through holographic duality |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-018-0075-2 |journal=Nature Physics |language=en |volume=14 |issue=6 |pages=573–577 |doi=10.1038/s41567-018-0075-2 |arxiv=1708.09393 |bibcode=2018NatPh..14..573U |issn=1745-2481}}</ref>

== Example ==
[[File:Reflected_entangling_surface_for_two-sided_black_hole.png|right|frameless|Reflected entangling surface for a two-sided Schwarzschild black hole]]
A simple illustration of the conjecture arises in the holographic dual of a two-sided [[Wormhole|eternal black hole]], described by the [[Thermal quantum field theory|thermofield]] double (TFD) state in a CFT. The left and right CFTs are individually in a [[Gibbs state]], while the combined system is in a pure entangled state. The dual spacetime is the two-sided [[Schwarzschild metric|Schwarzschild black hole]] geometry, which encodes the correlations between the two CFTs.

Consider a bipartition <math>A:B</math> of the left CFT. The Ryu-Takayanagi surface for <math>A\cup B</math> in the bulk spacetime is the black hole [[Schwarzschild radius|horizon]], to which the entanglement wedge <math>\mathcal{W}_{AB}</math> extends. As the right CFT (on <math>A^\star\cup B^\star</math>) is the canonical purification of the left CFT,

<math>S_R(A:B) = S_{\text{TFD}}(AA^\star)</math>.

The Ryu-Takayanagi minimal surface <math>A\cup A^\star</math> is shown in blue, which is exactly double the minimal cross-section of <math>\mathcal{W}_{AB}</math>.

<math>S_\text{TFD}(AA^\star) = 2\text{Area}(E_W) </math>.

As the former can be obtained by reflecting <math>E_\mathcal{W}</math> about the horizon, these surfaces are also called reflected minimal surfaces.
